# Corrected-prefetch lower-budget screen: useful-gain gate fails

Both native arms complete the frozen ten-GB workloads in [[sources/runs/2026/10/2026-10-06-candidate-correction-lowbudget-preparation]]. All timing eligibility and physical gates pass. Committed token IDs and text match exactly for all three workloads; the coding answer completes in both arms. The short-workload ratio fails the prospectively required improvement, so this screen earns no confirmation or product promotion. Preserve the smaller observed gains; do not call the correction slower or numerically wrong.

The collector fails after the corrected arm completes because its frozen helper predates the accepted corrected resource identity. The emitted identity is the explicitly charged profile already built and functionally checked before this experiment. A separate mechanical replay uses the already committed current validator. Its only change from the frozen helper is one exact mapping from the native corrected protocol to `affine3-native-corrected-memory-v1`; every other imported helper is byte-identical. No workload, numerical check, physical limit, timing exclusion, metric formula or success threshold changes. All completed receipts and the failed coordinator remain unchanged; neither model is rerun. The separate replay protocol and result are captured below.

This is one complete pair, not medians or an exact Auto qualification. It measures correction within native three-bit, not a new contemporaneous comparison against original four-bit. It does not measure the fourteen-GB configuration whose earlier admission refused. Small gains at this lower budget leave a large gap to the full speed target; the failed practical screen closes this scoped transfer route without another budget sweep. Reopen only for a materially stronger, evidence-backed mechanism. Original remains the supported/default pack.
